shape.name: Shape K - Vocabulary Development (Retrieval-Focused)
shape.description: Vocabulary lesson built on the research consensus: words are presented explicitly in context, then met repeatedly through spaced retrieval practice and varied input before generative productive use.
shape.pedagogical_justification:
Research on L2 vocabulary instruction converges on four principles that this shape operationalises.

(1) Selection: teach high-frequency, useful words (Nation, 2017; Nation & Waring, 1997).

(2) Explicit first meeting in context: an efficient initial encounter (brief meaning, form, pronunciation, phonemic script) gives learners something to retrieve later (Alizadeh, 2016; Nation, 2017).

(3) Retrieval and spacing: retrieval strengthens the form-meaning link, and spaced repetition beats massed repetition for long-term retention (Kim & Webb, 2022; Nation, 2017).

(4) Varied meetings and generative use: meeting a word in new contexts and using it productively deepens processing (Laufer & Hulstijn, 2001; Kim, 2011).

The lesson opens with a retrieval diagnostic (entry ticket) that sets the learning agenda and feeds the recycling stage.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use [target vocabulary] to [function] in the context of [topic].

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use numbers and measurements vocabulary (amount, average, length, height, width, weight, probability, percentage, sequence, sum) to discuss data and school life.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
17-08-26
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B2
Lesson Shape:
K (Vocabulary Development)
Materials:
Oxford Discover Futures 3, Unit 5 (Discover vocabulary), p. 120, slideshow, dialog audio, entry ticket worksheet
Assessment:
Entry ticket scores, retrieval activities, generative task observation
Systems:
Vocabulary

stages.stage_aim: To retrieve current vocabulary knowledge and set the learning agenda
procedure: Hand out the Vocabulary Levels Test (20 items, B1-C1). Set the 5-minute timer on the entry-ticket slide.
Students complete the test individually.
Display the answer slides (1-10, 11-20). Students swap and mark. Collect scores for feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To activate schema and set the numeracy context
procedure: Show the splash slide. Ask: What do you see? Where do you meet numbers every day? Let students speculate.
Advance to the title slide: How well do you know your numbers? Confirm the theme.
In pairs, students discuss: Where do you see numbers every day? Anchor the Opinion-Reason-Evidence structure.

stages.stage_aim: To present the ten target words clearly in context
procedure: Display the ten target words one at a time (phonemic script, then word, then context sentence).
Model pronunciation. Drill chorally and individually.
Elicit and check meaning with concept-checking questions (e.g. Is the average the biggest number or the typical number? Is the sum the result of adding or subtracting?).
Draw attention to form: measurements are paired with units (length in meters, weight in kilos).

stages.stage_aim: To meet the target words again in new contexts while listening
procedure: Present the Predict strategy (Do / Why / How) and try the demo.
Play the Numbers Around School dialog once. Students listen for gist: What is Leo doing? Check the answer.
Play the dialog again. Students answer four detail questions (homework average, percentage, classroom measurements, sequence). Check answers.
Point out the target words as they recur in the dialog (average, percentage, amount, sum, probability, length, width, height, weight, sequence).

stages.stage_aim: To retrieve form and meaning under controlled conditions
procedure: Exercise 1 (p. 120): students label the images with numbers and measurements words. 5-minute timer. Check answers.
Exercise 2 (p. 120): students complete the questions, then research the answers in pairs. 5-minute timer. Check answers.
Exercise 3 (p. 120): verb + preposition phrases (insisted on, searching for, occur in, apply to, belong to, appeared in). 4-minute timer. Check answers.
Exercise 4 (p. 120): money and budgeting words from the dialogues. 5-minute timer. Check answers.
Exercise 5 (p. 120): choose the correct words; true for you? 3-minute timer. Check answers.

stages.stage_aim: To use the target vocabulary productively in a freer task
procedure: In pairs, students discuss: How much money do you spend each week? Should students get a regular allowance? What is the average price of a school lunch?
They must use at least five target words (amount, average, budget, spend, save...). 5-minute timer.
Use the Opinion-Reason-Evidence scaffold. Pairs report one idea to the class.
Content feedback first, then language feedback on target word use.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate and set up spaced retrieval for the next lesson
procedure: Quick-fire retrieval round: the teacher says a definition, students say the word. 8 items.
Tell students the same words will reappear in next lesson's warm-up (spaced retrieval).
Exit question: Which word was most useful for you? Why?

metadata.topic: Numbers and numeracy - measurements, verb + preposition, money and budgeting
materials: Oxford Discover Futures 3, Unit 5 (Discover vocabulary), p. 120
Audio: Numbers Around School dialog (Ms. Rivera and Leo)
Entry ticket: Vocabulary Levels Test - M3 (20 questions) with answer key
metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, learners will be better able to use numbers and measurements vocabulary (amount, average, length, height, width, weight, probability, percentage, sequence, sum) to discuss data and school life.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: Learners will also have practiced listening for gist and detail in a school survey conversation, and consolidated verb + preposition phrases and money and budgeting vocabulary from the unit.

See the answer key on the last page of the handout: 1-D, 2-A, 3-A, 4-A, 5-C, 6-B, 7-D, 8-C, 9-D, 10-B, 11-B, 12-B, 13-C, 14-A, 15-C, 16-D, 17-B, 18-A, 19-D, 20-C.
Listening - Numbers Around School
Gist: Leo is doing a survey project about numbers.
Detail 1: The average student spends about an hour on homework every night.
Detail 2: Around sixty percent of students said that.
Detail 3: The classroom is nine meters long, seven meters wide, and about three meters high.
Detail 4: Leo organizes his numbers in a sequence, from smallest to largest.
Exercise 1 - Label the images
1. height - vertical arrow
2. width - horizontal arrow
4. length - ruler
5. amount - receipt price (90 c)
6. sum - receipt total ($7.49)
7. probability - rain chance (20%)
8. average - line graph curve
9. percentage - percent sign (%)
10. weight - kitchen scale
Exercise 2 - Complete the questions and research
1. The length of the Great Wall is about 21,196 km.
2. A soccer goal is 2.44 m high and 7.32 m wide.
3. The probability of rolling a five is 1 in 6 (about 16.67%).
4. An adult human brain weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kg.
5. A can of Coke contains about 39 grams of sugar.
6. About 50.4% of the world's population is male.
7. The average age of the world's population is about 30-31 years.
8. The next number in the sequence 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 is 19.
Exercise 3 - Verb + preposition
1. Dad insisted on paying for everyone.
2. Scientists have been searching for a cure for flu.
3. Brown eyes occur in a majority of the world's population.
4. The rules apply to everyone.
5. This jacket belongs to someone in the class.
6. My favourite actor has appeared in several movies this year.
Exercise 4 - Money and budgeting
1. They're talking about whether they can afford to take a taxi.
2. They're talking about how much she can lend.
3. They're talking about a debt.
4. They're talking about an allowance.
5. They're talking about a budget.
6. They're talking about a sale.
Exercise 5 - Choose the correct words
1. I earn money by doing jobs around the house.
2. I love going to the sales to look for bargains.
3. I don't spend much money on music each month.
4. I save about $20 every month.
5. I get an allowance of $100 every month.
6. The shoes I'm wearing today cost more than $60.
